Do you want to understand how a-kassa works before you need it? Good timing, because that is exactly when you can still do something about it. This text explains what separates a-kassa from a trade union, what is checked when you apply, and what happens if you are not a member.

## A-kassa and a trade union are not the same thing

It is easy to mix them up, because in practice they often go together. The trade union represents you against your employer: it negotiates pay, watches over your terms of employment, and gives legal support in a dispute. A-kassa is an insurance – an association you pay a fee to, which can then pay you compensation if you become unemployed and meet the conditions. You can be a member of an a-kassa without being in a trade union, and the other way around. Most a-kassor are linked to a profession or industry, but there are also a-kassor open to everyone, no matter what job you have.

## Why you need to be a member before you become unemployed

This is the most common misunderstanding, and the most expensive one. A-kassa is an insurance, and like most insurance, you cannot take it out after the damage has already happened. You cannot join an a-kassa on the day you are let go and expect compensation as if you had been a member for a long time. How long you have been a member when you become unemployed decides the level of your compensation. A person who has been a member for a long time gets the highest level. A person who has been a member for a shorter time gets a lower level. A person who joined very recently, or is not a member at all, gets the lowest level. You cannot fix this afterward by staying in the a-kassa.

If you are unsure whether you are a member, or since when, you can find that on your a-kassa's membership pages when you log in with BankID.

## Two things are checked: the income condition and your time as a member

Since autumn 2025 Sweden has a new law on unemployment insurance. The most important change: your right to compensation is based on what you have earned, not on how many hours you have worked. When you apply for compensation, a-kassa checks two separate things.

- **The income condition** (inkomstvillkor) – whether you have earned enough from work in the time before you became unemployed. This condition decides whether you get any compensation at all. It is checked whether you are a member or not. A-kassa gets the income information from Skatteverket (the Swedish Tax Agency), so what counts is the salary your employer has actually reported.
- **Your time as a member** – how long you have been a member up until you became unemployed. This decides which compensation level you get.

The older rule, called the work condition (arbetsvillkor), was based on hours worked. It no longer exists. If you read a text that talks about the work condition or a basic amount, it describes the old rules.

The level and the length of what you can get is then calculated based on your previous income during a period before you became unemployed. Exactly how that calculation is done, and which amounts and time limits apply right now, change from time to time through political decisions. Always check the current rule with your a-kassa instead of relying on something you read a year ago.

## Who decides, and who to turn to

It is your a-kassa that makes the decision about your compensation, not Arbetsförmedlingen. Arbetsförmedlingen confirms that you are registered and actively looking for work, which is information the a-kassa needs, but the actual assessment and payment is handled by the fund you are a member of (or Alfa-kassan, see below). If you disagree with a decision, you can ask your a-kassa to review it again. If that does not help, the Inspektionen för arbetslöshetsförsäkringen (IAF, the Unemployment Insurance Inspectorate) is the supervisory authority.

## If you are not a member: you can get compensation, but at the lowest level

If you are not a member of any a-kassa when you become unemployed, you are not completely without protection. If you meet the income condition, you can apply for compensation from Alfa-kassan even without membership. The compensation is still based on your previous income, but at the lowest level. There is no longer a fixed basic compensation that is the same for everyone. So it is the income condition, not the membership, that decides whether you get anything at all. Your membership, and how long you have had it, decides how large a part of your previous salary the compensation covers.

## How to check what applies to you

This text describes how the system works, not the current amount, number of days, or percentage, because those change, and an outdated number can do more harm than none at all. For what applies to you, right now:

- Log in to your a-kassa and read the conditions for your situation.
- If you do not know which a-kassa you belong to, or need to choose one: [Alfa-kassan](https://alfakassan.se) accepts everyone who does not belong to a profession-specific fund.
- If you are unsure about a decision, ask your case worker at the a-kassa to explain what was checked, not just what the result was.
- Register with [Arbetsförmedlingen](https://arbetsformedlingen.se) if you have not already, because that is part of the information your a-kassa needs.

## What should you do now

If you still have a job: check that you are a member of an a-kassa today, not on the day you are let go. If you are already unemployed: register with Arbetsförmedlingen on your first day without a job, and contact your a-kassa the same week to find out exactly what is required in your situation.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I have to be in a trade union to get a-kassa?
No. A-kassa and trade union membership are two separate memberships. You can be a member of an a-kassa without belonging to a trade union.

### Can I switch a-kassa if I change my profession?
Yes, you can join a different a-kassa. Ask the new fund how any previous membership time is counted – the rules for that differ depending on your situation.

### What happens if I become unemployed the same day I join?
Then you have not built up any time as a member, and you get the lowest compensation level. If you meet the income condition, you still have the right to compensation at that level.
summary_en: The difference between a-kassa and a trade union, why you need to be a member before you become unemployed, and what is checked when you apply.
title_en: How a-kassa (unemployment insurance) works – membership and conditions

The activity report is the document that keeps your benefit payments going month by month, and it is easy to make a mistake without noticing until it is too late. Here we go through what counts, how to describe it, and what happens if you miss it.

## What the activity report actually is

The activity report is your own account to Arbetsförmedlingen (the Swedish Public Employment Service) of what you have done to get closer to a job during the past period. It is not a formality you fill in just for the sake of it. It is the basis that Arbetsförmedlingen sends on to your a-kassa (Swedish unemployment insurance fund), or to Försäkringskassan (the Swedish Social Insurance Agency) if you receive aktivitetsstöd (activity support), and it is this basis that decides whether your payment continues. No report, no basis, no automatic payment.

## What counts as an activity

The activity report is about what you actually did, not what you plan to do. What normally counts:

- Jobs you applied for, with the company, position, and date.
- Contacts you made with employers, including unprompted ones.
- Meetings with recruiters, staffing agencies, or your network.
- Education, courses, or internships that are part of your plan.
- Activities you agreed on with your case officer in your action plan.

What does not count is a vague statement like "applied for jobs all week" without being able to show what. The case officer needs to see a concrete action, not an intention.

## How to describe an activity so it is good enough

Write as if someone else needs to follow what you did without asking you. That means including:

- **What** you did: applied for a job, went to a meeting, took a course.
- **Where**: which company, which education provider, which platform.
- **When**: which date.

Three lines per activity are plenty. It is better to have several clear lines than one long summary that cannot be checked.

## When it is due, and why the window matters

The activity report is submitted once a month, within a fixed window that Arbetsförmedlingen sets for you personally, which you can see on Mina sidor (My Pages). The window is not a suggestion. If you submit late, or not at all, it counts as not having met your obligation, even if you actually did search for jobs that month. The system only sees the report, not what you actually did if it is not written down.

## What happens if you miss it

Missing an activity report, or submitting one that is too thin, starts a chain of consequences at Arbetsförmedlingen that can, in turn, affect your benefit payments. Exactly what that chain looks like, and how serious the first miss is judged to be, changes from time to time through policy decisions, so we do not list the exact steps here. What you need to know is the principle: the more times you miss it, the more serious the consequence, and eventually your payment can stop completely until you meet the requirements again.

If you have a valid reason – illness, technical problems, an urgent family matter – contact Arbetsförmedlingen as soon as you can. A reason you flag in time carries more weight than one that comes afterward without explanation.

## The trick: keep notes as you go, never try to reconstruct later

What makes the activity report stressful is almost always the same thing: it gets put off until the last day, and then you suddenly have to remember a whole month. Instead, make it a habit to write down every job you apply for, every contact you make, on the same day you do it – in a notes app, a calendar entry, or a diary. When the report is due, the work is already done, you just copy it in. This saves time, and it makes the report more credible, because the details are fresh instead of guessed.

## What should I do now

Create a simple routine: every time you apply for a job or make a contact, write it down right away, with the company, position, and date. Check your reporting window on Mina sidor at Arbetsförmedlingen so you know exactly when it opens and closes. And if something happens that means you cannot submit on time, contact them before the deadline, not after.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is it enough that I applied for jobs, without writing down what?
No. The case officer needs to see concretely what you did. One line per job application with the company and date is enough.

### What if I forgot to keep notes during the month?
Go through your email inbox, your sent applications, and your calendar as best you can, and be honest if you do not remember everything. It is better to submit an incomplete but true report than to make things up.

### Do I still have to submit an activity report if I have received a job offer?
Yes, until you are actually deregistered as a job seeker. Let Arbetsförmedlingen know if your situation changes so they can update your status.
summary_en: What should be in the activity report, when it is due, and what happens if you miss it.
title_en: Activity Report to Arbetsförmedlingen – How to Do It

If you have a disability or a health condition, you have the right to accommodations that make it possible for you to do your job. Here is what you need to know.

## What Are Workplace Accommodations?

### Definition
Changes to the work environment, job duties, or working hours that make it possible for a person with a disability to do their job on equal terms with others.

### Examples of Accommodations
- Ergonomic equipment (a height-adjustable desk, a special chair)
- Assistive technology (screen readers, text-to-speech)
- Adjusted working hours
- The option to work remotely
- A quieter workplace
- Written instructions instead of spoken ones
- Regular breaks
- Changed job duties

## Your Rights

### The Discrimination Act
Employers must take "reasonable support and accommodation measures" so that people with disabilities can be in a comparable situation to people without disabilities.

### The Work Environment Act
The employer is responsible for a good work environment and must adjust the work to fit each person's needs.

### What Counts as "Reasonable"?
This is judged based on:
- The cost of the accommodation
- The size and resources of the employer
- How long the employment lasts
- The effect on the employee

## Types of Disabilities and Common Accommodations

### Physical Disabilities
**Possible accommodations:**
- Accessible premises (elevator, ramps)
- Ergonomic equipment
- Adjusted work height
- A parking spot close to the entrance
- Help with heavy lifting

### Visual Impairment
**Possible accommodations:**
- Screen readers and text-to-speech
- Magnification software
- A braille display
- Better lighting
- Spoken instructions and meetings

### Hearing Impairment
**Possible accommodations:**
- A hearing loop in meeting rooms
- A text telephone
- Visual signals (instead of sound signals)
- Written communication
- A sign language interpreter for meetings

### Neuropsychiatric Disabilities (NPF)
**Possible accommodations for ADHD, autism, and others:**
- Clear, written instructions
- A fixed structure and routines
- A separate, quiet workspace
- Ear protection/headphones
- Regular breaks
- Visual planning tools
- Fewer interruptions
- Clear communication

### Mental Health Conditions
**Possible accommodations:**
- Flexible working hours
- The option to work from home
- An adjusted workload
- Regular contact with your manager
- Access to counseling/support

### Chronic Illness
**Possible accommodations:**
- Flexibility for doctor's appointments
- Adjusted physical workload
- The option to rest
- Working from home when needed

## How to Request Accommodations

### Step 1: Prepare
- Identify which accommodations you need
- Be specific – what would help?
- Bring any documentation (a doctor's certificate, an assessment)

### Step 2: Contact the Right Person
- Your direct manager
- The HR department
- The safety representative (if you are unsure)

### Step 3: Have a Conversation
**Be prepared to:**
- Explain the challenges you have (you do not have to share everything)
- Suggest specific solutions
- Be open to discussion
- Write down what you agree on

### An Example of How to Say It
> "I have a disability that makes it hard for me to concentrate in an open-plan office. I would like to discuss the possibility of a quieter workspace or using headphones."

### Step 4: Follow Up
- Try out the accommodations
- Review after a couple of weeks
- Make adjustments if needed

## Support from Arbetsförmedlingen (the Swedish Public Employment Service)

### Grants for Equipment
Employers can get a grant for:
- Work equipment
- Workplace accommodations
- A personal assistant

### Wage Subsidy
If your work capacity is reduced, the employer can get a wage subsidy as compensation.

### Support for a Personal Assistant
A grant for practical help from a colleague.

### SIUS Consultant
A special support person who helps with introduction at a new workplace.

### How to Apply
1. Contact Arbetsförmedlingen
2. Describe your needs
3. They will assess what support fits
4. The employer can then apply for the grant

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Do I Have to Disclose My Disability?
No, you are not required to disclose it. But if you need accommodations, the employer must know what you need (not necessarily the diagnosis).

### Can the Employer Say No?
Only if the accommodation is not "reasonable" – meaning it is unreasonably expensive or hard to carry out. They must explain why.

### What Do I Do If the Employer Refuses?
1. Ask for a written explanation
2. Contact the union if you are a member
3. Contact DO (the Equality Ombudsman)
4. Talk to Arbetsförmedlingen

### Can I Get Accommodations During Probation?
Yes, the same rights apply.

### Can Accommodations Be Withdrawn?
Not without a valid reason. If your needs change, the accommodations can be adjusted.

## Tips for Success

### Be Specific
Instead of: "I need help concentrating"
Say: "I would need my own room or noise-cancelling headphones"

### Focus on Solutions
Show that you have thought about how it could work.

### Get Help
- An employment counselor at Arbetsförmedlingen
- A trade union
- Advocacy organizations (DHR, Attention, SDR, and others)

### Keep Records
Keep written documentation of the accommodations you have agreed on.

## Resources

### Government Agencies
- **Arbetsförmedlingen** – support and grants
- **Försäkringskassan (the Swedish Social Insurance Agency)** – benefits
- **DO** – for discrimination cases

### Advocacy Organizations
- **Funktionsrätt Sverige** – umbrella organization
- **DHR** – physical disabilities
- **Attention** – NPF (neuropsychiatric disabilities)
- **Mind** – mental health
- **SDR** – deaf people
- **SRF** – people with visual impairments

### Information
- **1177.se** – health information
- **Arbetsmiljöverket (the Swedish Work Environment Authority)** – rules and guidelines

## Summary

- You have the **right** to reasonable accommodations
- Be **specific** about what you need
- **Get help** from Arbetsförmedlingen and others
- **Keep records** of what you agree on
- Do not hesitate to **remind** people of your rights

With the right accommodations, almost everyone can do a full and valuable job. Your challenges do not have to be an obstacle – often it is just about finding the right solutions.
summary_en: A guide to workplace accommodations – what types exist, how to request them, and what support you can get.
title_en: Workplace Accommodations – Your Options

Understanding the different types of employment helps you make informed choices and know what you are entitled to. Here is a complete guide.

## Overview: Types of Employment in Sweden

| Type | Time limit | Protection from termination | Most common for |
|-----|-----------------|------------------|---------------|
| Permanent | No | Strongest | Regular positions |
| Fixed-term | Yes | Limited | Projects, seasonal work |
| Temporary replacement | Yes | Limited | Covering for someone absent |
| Probationary | Max 6 months | Weakest | New employments |
| Hourly | Varies | Limited | Extra jobs |

## Permanent Employment (Fixed Employment)

### What is it?
An employment with no end date that continues until someone ends it.

### Advantages
- **Security:** Cannot be ended without a valid reason
- **Stability:** Predictable income
- **Development:** Long-term skills development
- **Loans:** Easier to get a mortgage and credit
- **Insurance:** Better terms in group insurance
- **Career:** Chance of promotion and growth within the company
- **Benefits:** Access to wellness allowances, a company car, and more

### Disadvantages
- Can be harder to get right away
- Less flexibility if you want to change jobs
- A longer notice period can feel binding
- Harder to negotiate large pay raises internally

### Notice period
- 1 month (under 2 years of employment)
- 2 months (2–4 years)
- 3 months (4–6 years)
- Up to 6 months for longer employment

### Termination
The employer must have a valid reason:
- Lack of work (reorganization, cutbacks)
- Personal reasons (serious misconduct)

You have seniority protection ("last in, first out").

### Your rights as a permanent employee

| Right | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| Written notice | The employer must give written notice at least 2 months before termination due to lack of work |
| Seniority rules | The principle "last in, first out" applies |
| Right of priority | If you were let go due to lack of work, you have the right to be rehired for 9 months |
| Reassignment | The employer must try to reassign you before termination |
| The union | The employer must negotiate with the union before termination |

## Fixed-Term Employment (Time-Limited)

### General fixed-term employment
- No special reason is needed
- Maximum 24 months within a 5-year period
- Becomes permanent if the limit is exceeded

### Temporary replacement (vikariat)
- You replace someone who is absent
- Lasts as long as the regular employee is away
- No maximum time limit

### Seasonal employment
- For work during a certain season
- Common in agriculture, tourism, and retail

### Project employment
- Tied to a specific project
- Ends when the project is finished

### Advantages of fixed-term employment
- Easier to get a foot in the door
- A chance to try out the workplace
- Can lead to a permanent position
- Flexibility
- A chance to try different industries
- Often intense experience and learning

### Disadvantages of fixed-term employment
- Uncertainty about the future
- Harder to plan your finances
- Can be harder to get a loan
- Less access to some benefits
- Can feel like a "second-class employee"

### Your rights with fixed-term employment

**You have the right to:**
- The same basic terms as permanent employees (pay, vacation, work environment)
- Information about open permanent positions with the employer
- To know the reason for the fixed-term employment
- Not to be discriminated against for being a fixed-term employee

**You do NOT have the right to:**
- Protection from termination during the contract period (unless otherwise agreed)
- Priority for rehiring (if you have worked less than 12 months)

## Probationary Employment

### What is it?
A trial period before permanent employment.

### Rules
- Maximum 6 months
- Can be ended by either party without giving a reason
- Automatically becomes permanent if no one ends it
- 2 weeks' notice if it is ended

### Tips for employees on probation
- Show commitment from day one
- Ask for feedback regularly
- Keep a record of what you have achieved
- Ask about expectations

### Your rights during probation

| You DO have the right to | You do NOT have the right to |
|------------------|----------------------|
| The same pay as advertised | An explanation if it is ended |
| Protection under work environment rules | Seniority protection |
| Vacation | Protection from termination |
| The terms of the collective agreement | |

### How to get through probation

**The first week:**
- Be on time every day
- Ask questions – it shows commitment
- Learn your colleagues' names
- Write down important routines and systems

**The first month:**
- Ask for a follow-up meeting after 2–4 weeks
- Ask: "What do you expect from me during the probation period?"
- Be proactive and suggest improvements
- Keep a record of what you have achieved

**The last month:**
- Remind your manager that the probation period is ending soon
- Ask for feedback: "How do you think it is going?"
- Ask directly: "Will my employment become permanent?"

## Hourly Employment

### What is it?
You are called in when needed and paid by the hour.

### Types
- **On-call employment:** The employer calls when there is a need
- **Intermittent employment:** Regularly recurring work

### Advantages
- Flexibility
- You can say no
- Good as an extra job
- Can be combined with studies
- A chance to try different workplaces

### Disadvantages
- No guaranteed income
- Uncertainty
- Harder to plan ahead
- Limited benefits
- Risk of being taken advantage of

### Your rights
- The same hourly pay as regular employees
- Vacation (often paid as an extra amount, at least 12%)
- Protection under work environment rules
- Sick pay (after 14 days of employment)

### Protection against misuse

**Rules since 2022:**
- If you have worked an average of at least 8 hours a week for 6 months, you have the right to request a more secure form of employment
- The employer must respond in writing within one month
- Repeated hourly employment can be converted to permanent employment

## Proof of Employment

### You have the right to written information about:
- Employer and workplace
- Job duties
- Type of employment
- Start date (and end date for fixed-term employment)
- Pay and benefits
- Working hours
- Notice period
- Collective agreement (if there is one)

### Tips
- Always ask for written proof of employment
- Read it carefully before you sign
- Keep a copy

### Checklist: What should the contract include?

**Basic information:**
- [ ] The employer's name and registration number
- [ ] Your title and job duties
- [ ] Type of employment (permanent, fixed-term, etc.)
- [ ] Start date
- [ ] End date (if time-limited)

**Pay and compensation:**
- [ ] Monthly salary or hourly pay
- [ ] When you get paid
- [ ] Overtime pay (or if it is included in the salary)
- [ ] Vacation pay (for hourly employment)
- [ ] Any bonuses or commissions

**Working hours:**
- [ ] Working hours per week
- [ ] Fixed or flexible hours
- [ ] Any on-call duty
- [ ] Overtime rules

**Vacation and leave:**
- [ ] Number of vacation days
- [ ] Rules for saved vacation days
- [ ] Any unpaid leave

**Other:**
- [ ] Notice period
- [ ] Any non-compete clause
- [ ] Pension agreement
- [ ] Insurance
- [ ] Collective agreement (if there is one)

## Negotiating Your Employment Contract

### What can you negotiate?

**Common to negotiate:**
- Pay (always!)
- Start date
- Working hours and flexibility
- Working from home/remote work
- Wellness allowance
- Extra vacation days

**Harder to negotiate:**
- Type of employment (but ask anyway)
- Pension terms
- Notice period

### Negotiation tips

**Before the negotiation:**
1. Research the market pay for the role (SCB [Statistics Sweden], Unionen, lönestatistik.se)
2. List your strengths and experience
3. Decide your "walk away point" – what is the minimum you will accept?
4. Prepare an answer to "why should we pay more?"

**During the negotiation:**
- Stay positive and professional
- Start with a higher request than you expect to get
- Listen carefully to the employer's arguments
- Be ready to compromise in the right way

**Negotiation phrases:**
- "Based on my experience and the market pay for similar roles, I expected..."
- "Is it possible to discuss the salary?"
- "I am very interested in the position. Is there room for negotiation?"
- "If the salary cannot be adjusted, are there other benefits we could discuss?"

### What should you never accept without asking?

- Lower pay than advertised
- A probation period longer than 6 months
- A non-compete clause without compensation
- Overtime without extra pay (unless it is clearly stated to be included in the salary)
- Unclear job duties

## Converting to Permanent Employment

### When does fixed-term employment become permanent?

**General fixed-term employment:**
Automatically becomes permanent if you have worked more than:
- 24 months within a 5-year period

**Temporary replacement (vikariat):**
Automatically becomes permanent if you have:
- Worked as a replacement for more than 24 months within 5 years
- OR worked as a replacement plus general fixed-term employment for a combined 24 months

### What to do if your employment should have converted
1. Add up your time
2. Contact your employer
3. In case of a dispute: contact the union or Arbetsdomstolen (the Labour Court)

### Increase your chances of a permanent position

**From fixed-term to permanent:**
- Deliver more than expected
- Be visible and engaged
- Build relationships with managers and colleagues
- Ask early about the chance of an extension
- Ask for feedback and follow-up meetings
- Make it clear that you want to stay

## Collective Agreement

### What is it?
An agreement between a trade union and an employer organization that gives better terms than the law requires.

### Advantages of a collective agreement
- Higher minimum pay
- Better pension (occupational pension)
- Extra pay during parental leave
- Longer vacation
- Insurance
- Overtime pay
- Structured salary talks

### How to check
Ask the employer: "Do you have a collective agreement? With which union?"

### What happens if there is no collective agreement?

**You lose out on:**
- A guaranteed occupational pension
- Extra insurance (TFA, AGS)
- Standardized pay increases
- The union's support in negotiations

**You have to negotiate yourself:**
- Pension contributions in the contract
- Pay increases every year
- Insurance
- Overtime pay

## Common Traps – and How to Avoid Them

### "We offer an internship with a chance of employment"
**Warning:** Unpaid work experience at a company (not arranged through Arbetsförmedlingen [the Swedish Public Employment Service]) is often illegal. You should be paid for your work.

### "Start your own company and invoice us"
**Warning:** This can be an attempt to avoid employer responsibilities. You would miss out on pension, insurance, and security.

### "We can't offer a permanent position right now, but maybe later"
**Tip:** Ask for a written promise with a timeline, or a clear plan for what is needed.

### "The pay is fixed – overtime is included"
**Tip:** Check that this is legally correct and that the pay actually covers the overtime.

## Questions to Ask When You Are Hired

- What type of employment is offered?
- How long is the probation period?
- What happens after the probation period?
- Is there a collective agreement?
- What are the chances of a permanent position?
- What notice period applies?
- What insurance is included?
- How is overtime handled?
- Is remote work possible?
- What do the career paths look like?

## Remember

- No type of employment is "bad" – they fit different situations
- Fixed-term employment is often a first step
- Always read your proof of employment carefully
- Ask if you are unsure about anything!
- You always have the right to negotiate
- Keep a written record of everything

**Need help?** Your employment counselor can review employment contracts and give you advice about your rights.
summary_en: A guide to different types of employment, their advantages, and what you need to think about.
title_en: Types of Employment – What Is the Difference?

The arbetsgivarintyg (employer's certificate) is the document your a-kassa (Swedish unemployment insurance fund) wants to see before you can get unemployment benefits, and the tjänstgöringsbetyg (reference letter / service certificate) is what you bring with you to your next employer. The two are often mixed up, but they do different things – and you do not automatically get either one just because you quit.

## What is an arbetsgivarintyg, really

The arbetsgivarintyg is what your a-kassa uses to work out whether you are entitled to benefits, and if so, how much. It should include things like the length and type of employment, your working hours, your pay, and why the employment ended. It is not a judgment of you as a person or an employee – just facts about the employment.

**Your former employer is legally required to provide an arbetsgivarintyg**, no matter whether you resigned, were let go, or finished a temporary cover position. This obligation always applies – not only when you have "earned" it.

## Tjänstgöringsbetyg and reference – two other documents, different purposes

Here they are one by one, since the three are easy to mix up:

| Document | What it shows | Who has the right to request it |
|---|---|---|
| Arbetsgivarintyg | Length of employment, working hours, type of employment, pay | Everyone – it's a legal right |
| Tjänstgöringsbetyg | An assessment of how you did the job | Strongest right if the workplace has a collective agreement, otherwise no guaranteed right by law |
| Referens | A person who can answer questions about you by phone or in person | No legal right – it depends on someone agreeing to do it |

So a tjänstgöringsbetyg is something you can **request**, not something that gets written automatically. If you want one, say so before you leave, while your manager still remembers what you did.

A reference, in turn, is not a document at all – it is a name and phone number for someone willing to answer when a future employer calls. Ask the person in advance – being called with no warning is uncomfortable for most people.

## How to request the certificate

There are three ways to do this, and you can combine them:

1. **Ask directly on your last working day or in an exit conversation.** This is the easiest option – you are already talking anyway, and it is fresh in everyone's memory.
2. **Use your a-kassa's digital service.** Most a-kassor have a feature for requesting an arbetsgivarintyg electronically, often linked to a shared service that the employer fills in.
3. **In writing, if you don't get a response.** Download the form, fill in what you can, and send a clear request by mail or email, so there is a written record that you asked.

## When the employer doesn't respond

Requests sometimes fall through the cracks, especially at smaller workplaces without a dedicated HR function. Follow these steps in order:

- **Follow up in writing**, even if your first contact was verbal. An email gives you a record you can point to later.
- **Set a reasonable reminder**, for example one week later, and keep the tone factual.
- **Get help from your trade union** if you are a member – this is exactly the kind of situation your membership is for.
- **Contact your a-kassa** and let them know you are waiting. They have seen this problem before and can sometimes suggest alternative documentation while you wait.

## If the company has gone bankrupt

If you can no longer ask your employer because the company no longer exists, it is not a dead end. A bankruptcy administrator (konkursförvaltare) takes over part of the employer's obligations during the bankruptcy process, and can often help with documentation. If you have saved your pay slips and employment contract, they can serve as support while you wait for a formal certificate – check with your a-kassa about what they can accept in this situation. This is exactly the kind of situation where it pays off to already have copies saved – see the next section.

## Why you should request it when you leave, not when you need it

The big mistake is waiting. Six months or a year later, your contact person may have changed jobs, the company may have changed owners, or the email address you had may no longer work. While you are still employed or have just left, everything is easy to access: the systems are the same, the people are the same, and no one has any reason to make things difficult. Request the arbetsgivarintyg and, if you want one, the tjänstgöringsbetyg at the same time as you hand in your keys or log out for the last time.

## What should you do now

If you recently left a job without requesting any of this – do it today, not once you actually need to send it to your a-kassa. Save digital copies so you do not have to track them down again. And write down the name and contact details of someone who can be a reference while you still have them easily at hand.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I need an arbetsgivarintyg to apply for a new job?
No. It is needed to apply for benefits from your a-kassa, not for a regular job application. But it is smart to have it on hand anyway – you never know when you will need to prove a previous employment.

### Can I get an arbetsgivarintyg if I was let go or resigned myself?
Yes. The obligation to provide the certificate applies no matter why the employment ended.

### What do I do if I don't have a tjänstgöringsbetyg from an old job?
Contact the employer and ask, even if some time has passed. Without a collective agreement there is no legal right to one, but many employers will still write it if you ask clearly and politely.
summary_en: What the employer's certificate and reference letter are for, how to request them, and what to do if a former employer does not respond.
title_en: Employer's Certificate and Reference Letter – How to Get Them

Many hiring processes include a test – sometimes an aptitude test, sometimes a personality test, sometimes both. Here is the difference between them, what they actually measure, and how to prepare without trying to figure out the "right" answer.

## Three kinds of tests – and what each one tries to answer

They are often mixed up, but they measure different things and should be judged differently:

| Test type | What it measures | What "good" means |
|---|---|---|
| Aptitude test | How you solve new problems – logic, numbers, words, patterns | More correct answers in less time, not prior knowledge |
| Personality test | How you tend to act in different situations – teamwork, care, initiative | There is no right answer, only a profile |
| Work sample | How you actually solve a task similar to the job | How you think, not just the final result |

They are often used together, late in the process, when the employer is already interested in you. A test is rarely the only thing that decides everything – it is one piece of information among several, along with the interviews and references.

## What a personality test really measures

A personality test asks how you tend to behave – how you make decisions, how you react to stress, how you work with others. There is no answer key. The question is never "are you doing the right thing" but "does this match who you are".

That is exactly why it is tempting to answer the way you think the employer wants to see. This almost always backfires. Most serious personality tests have **control questions** – the same statement worded in different ways, repeated several times in the test. If you answer inconsistently, or if you keep answering in a "socially desirable" way instead of truthfully, it shows up as its own measurement in the result. The person interpreting the test will not see that you are a good candidate. They will see that your answers cannot be trusted, which is worse than a profile that simply does not match the role perfectly.

So the simplest advice still holds: answer based on how you actually tend to act, not how you wish you were or what you think the job requires. A profile that does not fit a specific role is not a failure – it is information, for you too.

## How to prepare for an aptitude test – sensibly, not with panic

An aptitude test is not a knowledge check. You cannot memorize the "right answers" the night before. What actually helps:

- **Get familiar with the format.** Many test providers have practice questions on their website that show what the questions look like and how the time is set up. Knowing what to expect removes some of the nervousness that would otherwise eat into your time.
- **Practice under time pressure**, not only without it. The tests are often deliberately tight on time – that is part of what is being measured.
- **Read the instructions calmly** before you start, even if the clock is already running. Misunderstanding the type of question costs more time than the extra seconds it takes to read carefully.
- **Sleep and eat as you normally would.** A tired mind performs worse on tasks that need concentration, no matter how much you know.
- **Do not turn it into a performance you must get perfectly right.** Most tests are built so that almost no one answers everything correctly within the time limit – that is the whole point of setting a time limit.

## What you have the right to ask about

Before or during the process, you can always ask to know:

- **What the test measures** and why that particular trait or ability is relevant to the job.
- **How the result is used** – is it decisive, or one piece of information among several?
- **Feedback on your result**, no matter how the process ends. This is a reasonable question to ask, not a sensitive one.
- **How the data is handled** – how long it is kept and who sees it.

No serious recruiter will be put off by you asking. On the contrary, these questions show that you take the process seriously.

## If the test situation does not suit you

If you have dyslexia, ADHD, or high test anxiety, for example, the test situation itself can mean the result does not show your real ability. It is reasonable to contact the recruiter beforehand and ask about accommodations – more time, a different format, or the chance to take the test in a calmer setting. It is better to ask one time too many than to go into a test you already know will measure the wrong thing.

## What should I do now

If you have a test booked: find out what type it is, check if the provider has practice questions, and schedule the test itself for a time when you are actually well-rested – not right after a long workday if you can choose. Afterward, no matter the outcome, ask for feedback. It will tell you more about what the role actually required than you could guess on your own.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I say no to a test?
You can always ask why the test is being used and what happens if you choose not to take it. The answer varies between employers and roles – for some jobs, the test is a natural part of the process, for others it is optional. Ask the recruiter directly.

### Are my test results saved?
Yes, usually for a period after the process ends. You have the right to know how long and why – ask if it is not stated in the information you received.

### What if I have reading or writing difficulties, or a diagnosis that affects how I perform on tests?
Contact them before the test and ask about accommodations. It is more common than you might think for test providers to offer alternative formats.

### Does a poor result mean I do not fit into the job market?
No. It means that this particular profile did not match this particular role. A test measures a snapshot in one specific situation, not your ability as a whole.
summary_en: The difference between aptitude tests, personality tests, and work samples, what they measure, and how to prepare without trying to guess the right answer.
title_en: Work Psychology Tests – What They Actually Measure

Work training (arbetsträning) means that for a period of time, you spend time at a workplace and practice work tasks and a working day as a whole, without it being a job and without being paid for it. The purpose is to build up your working hours, stamina, and endurance at a pace you can manage – not to perform at full capacity from the start.

## What work training actually is

You come to a workplace, often just a few hours or days a week to begin with, and do work tasks together with, or under the guidance of, someone who already works there. There is no performance requirement in the way there is in a regular job – the point is for you to try out how it feels to be there, at that pace, doing these tasks.

Work training is planned by the employer or Arbetsförmedlingen (the Swedish Public Employment Service) together with Försäkringskassan (the Swedish Social Insurance Agency), which assesses whether it is a suitable form of rehabilitation for your situation.

## It is not employment

This is important to understand, because it affects everything else:

| | Work training | Employment |
|---|---|---|
| Salary | No – another form of compensation may apply | Yes |
| Employment contract | No | Yes |
| Performance requirements | Adapted, no fixed requirement | Yes, according to the role |
| Notice period | Does not apply in the same way | Yes |
| Purpose | Try out and build up ability | Carry out a job |

Not being employment does not mean it is worth less. It means the time has a different purpose – to find out what works, before anyone expects it to already work.

## The purpose: building up what carries you

Work training is often aimed at people who have been away from working life for a long time, or who do not yet know how a normal working day feels in the body. It is about gradually increasing your working hours and workload, while seeing which tasks go well and which need more support or a different approach.

It is also a chance to test things in reality that are hard to know in advance: how much a work shift takes out of you, whether a certain type of task suits you, whether the pace of the workplace is something you can handle.

## What you can expect from the supervision

Work training without real supervision is just standing around and waiting at a workplace. You have the right to expect:

- **A clear contact person** at the workplace you can turn to, not just "someone on the team."
- **A review of what is expected** before you start a task, not afterward when something has gone wrong.
- **Regular check-ins** on how it is going – not just one conversation at the start and one at the end.
- **That the workload is actually adjusted** if you say it is too high, not just noted down.

If none of this is happening, it is something to raise with whoever planned the work training – your caseworker at Försäkringskassan or Arbetsförmedlingen, not only the workplace itself.

## Does it lead to a job? The honest question

Everyone doing work training asks this question, and the honest answer is: it depends on why the placement was chosen. Work training that is connected to a real possibility of employment – where the employer has a need and sees you as a possible candidate – is a very different thing from a placement that only exists to fill a schedule.

What you can influence:

- **Ask directly, early on**, whether there is a possible job at the end of it, or whether the placement was chosen for other reasons.
- **Ask for the work training to be placed where the need actually exists** – with an employer who could realistically hire you, not just one who happens to have an open spot.
- **Be clear about what you want to get out of it**, to your caseworker, so the next step is planned with that in mind instead of just becoming the next activity on the list.

Work training on its own is no guarantee of a job. But chosen well, and with a clear conversation about the purpose from the start, it is one of the more concrete ways to get closer to employment – not just an activity to check off.

## Who decides

Försäkringskassan assesses whether work training is a suitable measure for you, often in coordination with Arbetsförmedlingen and the workplace in question. The decision is based on your ability to work and what would be needed to increase it – not on a diagnosis.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do I get any compensation during work training?

There are forms of compensation linked to rehabilitation, but the exact terms and amounts change – ask your caseworker at Försäkringskassan what applies to you.

### Can I say no to a work training placement?

Yes, and it is better to say so clearly than to go through a placement you already know is not right for you. Explain why, so the next suggestion can be a better match.

### How long does work training last?

It varies and is decided based on your needs, not a fixed template. Ask your caseworker what applies in your case.

## What to do now

Ask your caseworker at Försäkringskassan or Arbetsförmedlingen to explain why that particular workplace is being suggested, and ask directly whether there is a job at the end of it. Consider writing down how the shifts feel week by week – it makes it easier to see whether the workload is actually increasing, and it is something you can bring to your next check-in.

Read more about work-related rehabilitation at [forsakringskassan.se](https://www.forsakringskassan.se) and about work training through Arbetsförmedlingen at [arbetsformedlingen.se](https://arbetsformedlingen.se).
summary_en: Work training is not employment and does not pay a salary, but it can build up your working hours and stamina. Here is how to tell if the placement can actually lead somewhere.
title_en: Work Training – What It Is, and Whether It Leads to a Job

Many CVs are never seen by human eyes – they get filtered out by ATS systems. Here you will learn what an ATS is and how to get past the filter.

## What is an ATS?

ATS stands for Applicant Tracking System. It is software that:
- Receives and sorts applications
- Searches CVs for keywords
- Ranks candidates automatically
- Helps recruiters handle large numbers of applications

### Who uses an ATS?
- Almost all large companies
- Many medium-sized companies
- Recruitment agencies
- The public sector

### Common ATS systems
- Teamtailor (common in Sweden)
- Workday
- Taleo
- Greenhouse
- Lever

## How does an ATS work?

### Step 1: Parsing
The system reads your CV and tries to understand its structure:
- Name and contact information
- Work experience
- Education
- Skills

### Step 2: Keyword matching
The ATS compares the content with the job requirements:
- Does the candidate have the right education?
- Is the right experience there?
- Do the skills match?

### Step 3: Ranking
Candidates are ranked by how well they match. The highest-ranked candidates move on to human review.

## Common mistakes that kill your application

### 1. The wrong file format
❌ PDF with images and graphics
❌ Word with complex tables
✅ A simple PDF or .docx file

### 2. Creative layouts
❌ Columns and text boxes
❌ Icons and graphic elements
❌ Infographic-style CVs
✅ A simple, linear layout

### 3. Images and logos
❌ Profile photo
❌ Company logos
❌ Icons for contact information
✅ Text only

### 4. Missing keywords
❌ "Customer-focused" when the ad says "customer service"
❌ Your own wording for standard terms
✅ Use exactly the same words as in the job ad

### 5. The wrong structure
❌ Creative headings ("My journey")
❌ An unconventional order
✅ Standard headings: Work Experience, Education, Skills

## How to optimize your CV for an ATS

### 1. Use the right format
- Save it as .docx or a simple PDF
- Avoid graphic PDF creators
- Test copying the text – if it comes out messy, redo it

### 2. Keep the layout simple
- One column
- A standard font (Arial, Calibri, Times New Roman)
- Clear headings
- Bullet points without special symbols

### 3. Match keywords

**Do this:**
1. Read the job ad carefully
2. Mark all the requirements and skills
3. Include the exact wording in your CV
4. Use both abbreviations and full terms (for example, "CRM" and "Customer Relationship Management")

### 4. Use standard headings
- Summary / Profile
- Work Experience
- Education
- Skills
- Languages
- Certifications

### 5. Include hard facts
- Years of employment
- Company names
- Exact job titles
- Results you can measure

## Checklist: An ATS-friendly CV

- [ ] A simple layout without columns
- [ ] .docx or a simple PDF
- [ ] No images or graphics
- [ ] A standard font
- [ ] Standard headings
- [ ] Keywords from the job ad included
- [ ] Contact information in the text (not in a header/footer)
- [ ] No tables
- [ ] Dates in the format MM/YYYY or Month YYYY

## Test your CV

### The copy test
1. Select all the text in your CV
2. Copy it and paste it into Notepad
3. Is the text readable and in the right order?
4. If not – redo the layout

### Online tools
There are tools that check how ATS-friendly your CV is:
- Jobscan
- Resume Worded
- TopResume

## Balance: ATS vs. human reader

Remember that your CV needs to pass BOTH the ATS and human eyes:

**For the ATS:**
- Keywords
- A simple structure
- The right format

**For people:**
- Readable and clear
- Shows your personality
- Tells your story

## Frequently asked questions

**Should I have two different CVs?**
No, but adjust the content for each application. Add relevant keywords.

**Do creative CVs never work?**
They can work for small companies without an ATS, or in creative industries. But always have an ATS-friendly version ready too.

**Can I cheat by hiding keywords in white text?**
No! Hiding text in white is detected and will disqualify you immediately.

## Summary

ATS systems are a reality – accept it and adapt:
1. Use a simple format and layout
2. Match keywords from the job ad
3. Test that your CV is readable as plain text
4. Keep the balance between ATS optimization and human readability

An ATS-friendly CV dramatically increases your chances of being seen by a recruiter.
summary_en: Most large companies use ATS systems that filter CVs automatically. Learn how to optimize your CV so it does not get filtered out.
title_en: ATS Systems – How to Get Your CV Past the Robots

A background check often causes more worry than it deserves — and for certain jobs, especially in schools and care work, a criminal record extract is a completely normal part of the process. Here is what an employer is actually allowed to check, how a record extract works, and how to handle it if there is something on your record.

## What an employer may check — and what needs your consent

A background check may only cover what is actually relevant to the job. An employer can contact references you have given, verify degrees or employment certificates, and, for certain roles, run a credit check or request a criminal record extract. Anything that is not relevant to the role should not be collected just because it is possible — the more sensitive the information, the clearer the connection to the job needs to be.

You have the right to know what information is being collected, why, and how it will be used. If a check feels unjustified for the role — ask directly why it is being done. That is a reasonable question, not a suspicious one.

A recruiter searching for your name online or looking at your public LinkedIn profile is hard to stop and happens often in practice. More systematic checks of social media, especially anything that is not public or has nothing to do with work, are in a legal gray area, and the Diskrimineringsombudsmannen (DO, the Equality Ombudsman) and Integritetsskyddsmyndigheten (the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection) have raised concerns about this.

## Criminal record extracts — who requires them, and how you order one

In some industries, a criminal record extract is a requirement, not a choice made by the employer — most clearly in schools and preschools, but it also happens in other parts of health and social care. The rules about exactly which crimes are shown and how long an extract stays valid change from time to time, so you should trust Polismyndigheten's (the Swedish Police Authority's) own information, not a memory of how it worked the last time you applied for a job.

The process is the same no matter the industry: **you order your own extract from Polismyndigheten**, not the employer. You are the one with the right to see what is written in it. The employer may look at the extract and note that it has been shown — but may not keep it, copy it, or write down what was in it.

## Do I have to hand it over unopened?

Many employers ask to see the extract in an unopened envelope, but this is a common routine rather than a legal requirement — you have the right to open and read your own extract before showing it, and for certain professions, including school, preschool, and parts of LSS (support and service for people with certain disabilities) and HVB (residential care homes for children and young people) work, you always have this right explicitly. If you are unsure what applies to your own situation, Polismyndigheten's own page about record extracts has the correct answer, not this text.

## If you have a mark on your record — here is how to handle it

There is nothing to be ashamed of in wondering how a past conviction affects a job application. Here is how to think about it, without being hard on yourself:

### When it actually matters

An entry in the criminal record matters when it has a clear connection to the job — a financial crime and a role with responsibility for cash, a crime against a person and a role that involves working alone with children or vulnerable adults. An old entry with no connection to the content of the role carries different weight, and for many jobs it does not show up at all in the extract that is requested, because different types of extracts show different information depending on what they are meant for.

### Bringing it up yourself, at the right time

If a mark shows up in a record extract without you having said anything about it beforehand, the question in the room suddenly becomes "why didn't you tell me" instead of "what happened." That is almost always a weaker position to negotiate from.

The right time to bring it up yourself is when the process has gone far enough to feel serious — not in the first email, but ideally before a record extract is requested, if you know the industry requires one. Keep it short: what happened, roughly when, and what is different now. You do not need to explain the whole situation or defend yourself in detail. A short, direct sentence carries more weight than a long explanation that sounds rehearsed.

What you gain by taking the initiative is that you control when and how the conversation happens. If you wait for the employer to find it on their own, you control nothing.

## What to do now

If you know that a job you are applying for requires a record extract — order it from Polismyndigheten in good time, so you are not left without it when it is requested. If you have an entry that might be relevant, prepare a short, direct way of explaining it in advance instead of improvising in the moment. If you are unsure whether a check an employer wants to do is reasonable — ask why, that is always a fair question.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can an employer require a criminal record extract for any job?
No, there must be a clear connection to the role — required by law for certain professions, justified by the content of the role for others. If the requirement feels unjustified, ask why it is being made.

### Can an employer keep my record extract?
No. The employer may look at it and note that it was shown, but may not copy, scan, or keep it.

### Does every extract show everything in the criminal record?
No. Different types of extracts — for example for schools compared with other industries — show different kinds of information depending on what the extract is meant for. Polismyndigheten's page explains which type applies to your situation.

### What happens if I say nothing and it comes out anyway?
This rarely helps your case compared with telling them yourself. It does not mean everything is lost — but the conversation will be different, and you will have less control over how it is framed.
summary_en: What a background check may include, how to get a criminal record extract, and how to bring up a mark on your record yourself — at the right time.
title_en: Background Checks — What an Employer Is Allowed to Check

Staffing agencies can be an excellent way into the job market. They help you find work, and you gain experience from different workplaces. Here is how it works.

## What is a staffing agency?

A staffing agency hires you and "leases" you out to other companies. You are employed by the staffing agency, but you work at their clients' workplaces.

### Common staffing agencies in Sweden
- Manpower
- Adecco
- Randstad
- Academic Work
- StudentConsulting
- Poolia
- Proffice

## How does it work?

### 1. You register
Create a profile on the staffing agency's website. Upload your CV and answer questions.

### 2. Interview with the staffing agency
They get to know you, your skills, and what you are looking for.

### 3. Matching
When an assignment fits your profile, they contact you.

### 4. Interview with the client company
You are often interviewed by the company where you will work.

### 5. You start working
You work at the client company but are employed by the staffing agency.

## Advantages

### Easier to get a job
- Staffing agencies have many contacts
- They do the work of finding opportunities
- A lower threshold for employers to "try you out"

### Experience and variety
- Work at different companies
- Try different roles
- Build a broad network

### A path to permanent employment
- Many are offered permanent employment by the client company
- You get to show what you can do

### Flexibility
- Often shorter assignments
- Can suit students or those who want variety

## Disadvantages

### Uncertainty
- No guaranteed assignments
- Periods without work can occur

### Less sense of belonging
- You are not "one of them" at the workplace
- Can feel like an outsider

### Sometimes lower pay
- Can be lower than for directly employed staff
- But a collective agreement should protect you

## Your rights

### Equal treatment
By law, you should have the same basic terms as directly employed staff:
- Pay (at least according to the collective agreement)
- Working hours
- Vacation

### Collective agreement
Most reputable staffing agencies have a collective agreement that provides:
- Guaranteed pay between assignments (varies)
- Sick pay
- Pension
- Insurance

## Tips for success

### Register with several
- Increases your chances
- Different agencies have different assignments

### Be available and flexible
- Answer quickly when they call
- Be open to different assignments
- Short notice can work in your favor

### Do a good job
- Client companies give feedback
- Good feedback = more assignments
- Can lead to permanent employment

### Stay in touch
- Call and remind them you're available
- Update your profile
- Be proactive

### Network on assignments
- Build relationships at every workplace
- You never know who might help you later

## Frequently asked questions

**Is it legitimate?**
Yes, if you choose established companies. Check that they have a collective agreement.

**Can I decline an assignment?**
Yes, but don't decline too often – or you'll get fewer offers.

**What happens between assignments?**
It depends on your contract. Some have guaranteed pay, others don't.

**Can I become permanently employed at the client company?**
Yes! It is common, and often the intention from the start.

## Warning signs

Be cautious if:
- They lack a collective agreement
- They want you to invoice them (F-tax status, a Swedish self-employment tax registration, without having your own registered company)
- The terms are unclear
- They charge you money

## Summary

Staffing agencies can be a good strategy:
1. **Register** with several reputable agencies
2. **Be flexible** and available
3. **Do a good job** on every assignment
4. **Network** and build relationships
5. **See it as an opportunity** to show what you can do

For many people, it is the springboard to permanent employment.
summary_en: How do staffing agencies work? Advantages, disadvantages, and how to maximize your chances.
title_en: Staffing agencies – your shortcut into the job market

It is often said that certain industries are "crying out for people". The problem with that phrasing is that industries do not hire — occupations do. And two occupations that sit right next to each other in the same industry can have completely opposite conditions.

This text is about how to find the occupations where there actually is a way in for you. The figures are based on Arbetsförmedlingen's (the Swedish Public Employment Service) occupational barometer from June 2026 and the Labour Market Outlook for spring 2026. The next update of the occupational barometer comes in December 2026.

## Three words that mean different things

Arbetsförmedlingen puts a label on every occupation it assesses. The labels look similar at a quick glance, but differ in what they mean for you:

- **Shortage** — employers find it hard to recruit, and there are few available people in the occupation. Often occupations that require a license, certification, or long education.
- **Paradox** — employers find it hard to recruit *at the same time as* there are unemployed people, part-time workers, or people leaving the occupation.
- **Balance** — supply and demand are roughly even.
- **Surplus** — more people are seeking the occupation than employers need.

In the June 2026 assessment, 205 occupations had a national rating. Of these, 57 were rated as shortage, 77 as balance, 41 as surplus, and 30 as paradox.

## Paradox occupations are usually the realistic way in

If you have been away from working life for a while, it is easy to fixate on the shortage list. But a pure shortage of specialist doctors or engineers with a university degree says nothing about your chances — those occupations are hard to recruit for precisely because they require years of education you do not have.

Paradox occupations are a different matter. There, recruitment problems exist *together with* an actual supply of workers. That means employers are looking, and that people with a background like yours actually do get in.

Among the occupations rated as paradox in June 2026 are, among others:

- Assistant nurses in home care, home healthcare, elderly care, and disability support
- Care workers and support workers, personal assistants
- Treatment assistants and social education workers
- Cleaners
- Restaurant and kitchen assistants, waiters, pizza bakers, bakers, and pastry chefs
- Head chefs, sous chefs, maîtres d'
- Welders and gas cutters
- Bricklayers and tile setters
- Forestry workers, landscape gardeners, growers, and livestock keepers
- Hairdressers, massage therapists
- Vocational teachers

The list is not complete, and it looks different in different parts of the country.

## The trap: two titles that sound alike

This is the most important part of this whole text, and it is also where most advice goes wrong.

| Rated as shortage or paradox | Rated as surplus |
|---|---|
| Assistant nurse | Care assistant |
| Software and systems developer, IT architect | System administrator |
| Chef | Retail sales assistant, cashier |
| Construction worker, concrete worker | Warehouse and terminal staff, forklift operator |

Care assistant and assistant nurse end up in opposite categories even though they work in the same corridor. System administrator and software developer, likewise. A text that stops at "healthcare needs people" or "there are jobs in IT" therefore sends roughly half of its readers in the wrong direction.

The conclusion is easy to state and a little harder to follow: **check the occupation, not the industry.** Before you spend several months on an education or a career push, look up the exact occupational title in Arbetsförmedlingen's occupational barometer and see what it says.

## Where the shortage is greatest right now

Counted by occupational field, these had the largest share of shortage occupations in June 2026:

- Installation, operation, and maintenance — 7 of 11 assessed occupations
- Healthcare — 14 of 29
- Technical work — 6 of 14
- Construction — 6 of 17, and not a single surplus occupation
- Data and IT — 4 of 10
- Education — 4 of 11

The largest share of surplus occupations was found in culture, media, and design (6 of 9), sales, purchasing, and marketing (6 of 14), and administration, finance, and law (4 of 19).

If you mention data and IT, it is worth being precise: the figures above are about *today's* recruitment problems. Arbetsförmedlingen makes a separate assessment of the future gap, in which IT occupations are not among those with the largest expected shortfall. These are two different questions, and they have different answers.

In the spring 2025 assessment, the shortage was also more concentrated in the counties of northern Sweden. Where you live matters.

## What "shortage" actually measures

It is easy to hear the word shortage as a verdict. It is not — it is a measurement definition.

An occupation is rated as having recruitment difficulties when the share of failed recruitment attempts is at least 15 percent. The rating is based on five factors: the share of failed recruitment attempts according to Arbetsförmedlingen's monthly survey of employers, the share of part-time workers, the share leaving the occupation, the unemployment level, and the rate of new recruitment. The occupations follow the official occupational classification at the four-digit level, which is exactly why the titles are so finely divided.

Knowing this makes the numbers easier to carry. "Shortage" means that a certain share of recruitments fail — not that anyone is guaranteed a job.

## What employers say they are missing

According to Arbetsförmedlingen's (the Swedish Public Employment Service) report Arbetsmarknadsutsikterna våren 2026, 51 percent of employers who had tried to recruit over the past six months reported running into one or more problems. More than one in four workplaces failed completely at a recruitment. It was hardest in the construction industry, where 40 percent of employers failed at least one recruitment.

The most common problem was **too few applicants with sufficient work experience**. This was true across all sectors except public services, where the wrong education dominated instead — a result of many occupations there being licensed occupations with formal education requirements. Employers also mentioned difficulty finding people with suitable personal qualities and sufficient Swedish language skills.

This says something useful about where your energy does the most good. When the obstacle is usually experience rather than education, that points toward internships, temporary positions, hours worked, and references — not automatically toward yet another course.

And when recruitment still struggles, the most common response is that the employer extends the recruitment period. The second most common is to lower the experience requirements. That this door sometimes opens is not a comfort, but it is a fact you can plan around: an employer who has been searching for a long time is more likely to look twice at you.

## How to use this

1. Choose a couple of occupational titles, not an industry.
2. Look up each title in the occupational barometer and see whether it is rated shortage, paradox, balance, or surplus.
3. Pay extra attention to the paradox occupations — that is where need and supply meet.
4. Ask your employment coach or Arbetsförmedlingen how things look in your specific county.

Demand is, incidentally, expected to increase in 177 of the assessed occupations over a five-year horizon, stay unchanged in 22, and decrease in 6. That is a forecast, not a promise — but the direction is worth knowing when you choose where to put your time.
summary_en: The difference between shortage occupations, paradox occupations, and surplus occupations — and why it decides where it is worth applying.

Writing a CV from scratch can be hard. Here are templates and examples to help you get started.

## Basic structure for all CVs

### 1. Contact details
- Name (large and clear)
- Phone number
- Email address (professional!)
- LinkedIn profile (optional)
- Location (optional)

### 2. Profile/summary
3-5 sentences summarizing:
- Who you are
- What you can do
- What you are looking for

### 3. Work experience
Reverse chronological order (most recent first)

### 4. Education
Reverse chronological order

### 5. Skills
- Skills
- Languages
- Certifications

## Template 1: For those with experience

**Profile:**
"Results-driven [occupation] with [number] years of experience in [area]. Strong in [key skill 1] and [key skill 2]. Looking for new challenges in [area] where I can contribute [what you offer]."

**Experience:**
"[Title] | [Company] | [Month Year] – [Month Year]
- Responsible for [area of responsibility]
- Achieved [result with numbers]
- Led [project/initiative] that resulted in [outcome]"

## Template 2: For those without experience

**Profile:**
"Motivated and eager-to-learn [title/education] with strong drive to develop within [industry]. Have good [skills] from [education/experience]. Looking for the opportunity to contribute and grow at [type of company]."

**Experience (replace with):**
- Internships
- Summer jobs
- Volunteer work
- School projects
- Personal initiatives

## Template 3: For a career change

**Profile:**
"[Occupation] with [number] years of experience in [current industry] who now wants to transfer my skills in [key skills] to [new industry/role]. Strong in [transferable skill] and [transferable skill]."

**Tips:**
- Highlight transferable skills
- Explain why you are changing direction
- Show genuine interest in the new field

## Template 4: For senior positions

**Profile:**
"Experienced [occupation] and leader with [number] years of documented success in [areas]. Specialized in [areas of expertise]. Have led teams of [size] and driven [types of projects]."

**Focus on:**
- Leadership and strategic work
- Results and business impact
- Larger projects and initiatives
- Industry network

## Examples of results (with numbers)

### Sales:
- "Increased sales by 25% during the first quarter"
- "Managed a customer portfolio worth 10 million kr"

### Project management:
- "Led a team of 8 people on a project worth 5 million kr"
- "Delivered 15 projects on time and within budget"

### Customer service:
- "Achieved 95% customer satisfaction"
- "Handled 50+ cases daily"

### Efficiency improvements:
- "Streamlined processes that saved 20 hours/week"
- "Reduced costs by 15%"

## Common mistakes to avoid

❌ General claims without evidence – "I am good at sales"
✅ Concrete results – "I increased sales by 20%"

❌ Too long – more than 2 pages
✅ Concise – 1-2 pages is perfect

❌ One CV for every job
✅ Tailored for each application

❌ Spelling mistakes and carelessness
✅ Proofread by you and someone else

## Download templates

You can download Word templates for all these variants in our CV builder. There you can also get automatic suggestions for wording based on your information!
